independence.temporaryProbeCustody: All malicious-pyc, wrong-hash, capability-forgery, registry-substitution, and lifecycle probes ran in memory or in automatically removed operating-system temporary directories. No candidate, checker, adjudication, v1 baseline, source authority, integration, claim, narrative, or sealing artifact was edited.
independence.reviewMethod: Hashes were recorded before substantive checker execution and rechecked after all probes. The source projection was reconstructed without importing the candidate checker. The exact checker bytes were then compiled into a fresh module namespace and attacked directly. Green authored controls were retained as checker behavior, not treated as independent proof.

verdict.summary: The v2 exact-source execution path closes the v1 cached-bytecode blocker, and the normal lifecycle, serialization, source-projection, and preservation checks pass. The capability repair remains forgeable: any code with the checker module can construct its own MintGateV2 and call the module-global mint helper, a context exposes its real gate through a callable method, and projection trusts the context-supplied gate and registry. Accepted contexts can therefore be minted without ingress or reservation, duplicated for an already-reserved RequestId, or made authoritative through a substituted registry. TRC-PF-02 is not closed.

method.decisionRule: A declared blocker is closed only if the exact successor implementation rejects independently constructed counterexamples within its claimed model boundary. One reproducible accepted construction path that bypasses ingress or reservation is blocking even when all authored controls are green.
method.sourceReconstruction: Parsed the exact pinned OPERABILITY v2 bytes with duplicate-key rejection and independently selected the declared REQUEST-ID-V1 paths without importing check-trusted-request-context-v2.py.
method.trustOrderingReview: Loaded the exact v2 checker byte buffer only after verifying its SHA-256, then exercised its actual _exec_pinned_source helper against an authentic source file accompanied by a timestamp-valid malicious pyc. A separate wrong-hash source contained an execution marker to test rejection-before-side-effect.
method.capabilityReview: Created capabilities and forgeries through the exact checker model rather than relying on _capability_probes. Tests included a newly constructed gate plus module mint helper, a substituted gate registry, real-gate extraction through the context accessor, duplicate minting, and minting an ID absent from the host reservation set.
method.normalCheckerUse: The three documented verification commands were run exactly as declared. Their exit codes describe authored-checker behavior and are not the acceptance verdict.

modelBoundaryApplicability.explanation: The decisive no-ingress probe uses normal construction and function calls exposed by the exact checker module. The gate-leak probe additionally uses a callable method deliberately defined on the capability. These are the same class of module-private access considered by the v1 finding and are not arbitrary memory writes or debugger compromise.

blockingFindings.finding: The registry is not an externally rooted provenance oracle. _MintGateV2 is freely constructible, _mint_context is a module-global callable that accepts any instance of that class, and _request_id normally trusts whichever gate the context itself supplies. A context also exposes its real mint gate through _gate_for_checker. The checker therefore replaces v1's global token with a self-authenticating, caller-constructible gate rather than establishing ingress provenance.

counterexamples.observed: _MintGateV2() plus _mint_context accepted and projected a canonical context without HostRequestIngressV2 or any reservation.
A forged exact-type object registered under its own newly constructed gate projected successfully.

The capability's _gate_for_checker method returned the real host gate; direct mint calls then created one distinct accepted duplicate for an already-reserved RequestId and one accepted context for an ID absent from the host reservation set.

blockingFindings.consequence: The executable oracle does not establish ingress-only minting, reservation-before-mint, collision uniqueness, registry-substitution resistance, or an exactly-one-field capability projection. The adjudication's ACCEPTED-AND-REPAIRED disposition for TRC-PF-02 is false for the exact v2 bytes, and normal-path lifecycle checks cannot compensate for bypasses around HostRequestIngressV2.
requiredRepair: Either narrow the executable evidence claim so the Python model is explicitly only API-shape illustration and excludes direct use of its module-private constructors, mint helpers, gate accessors, and registries, or replace the model with a provenance oracle rooted in authority that an input context cannot construct or self-supply.

Do not expose mint authority from the context. Projection must validate against independently held ingress/registry authority and an exact reservation-to-context binding rather than trusting context._gate_for_checker().

Prevent a newly constructed gate from satisfying mint authority and prevent the module mint helper from creating a projecting context unless the RequestId was reserved exactly once by the owning ingress.

Add retained negatives that actually register a forged object under a substituted gate, call the mint helper with a newly constructed gate, leak the real gate from a normal context, mint a duplicate context, and mint an unreserved ID. Each must reject with no reservation or registry side effect.
Retain PRODUCTION-CAPABILITY-IMPLEMENTATION and ATOMIC-RESERVATION-RUNTIME after repair; a Python model still cannot demonstrate the production Rust boundary.

The v1 required repair asked for a retained negative for every claimed construction route. The v2 forbidden list and TRC2-3 name stage, profile, and projection adapter, but the 20 declared adversarial controls contain no distinct stage, profile, or projection-adapter case; caller, sink, and provider still share one helper that discards origin and value.

Independent execution of the actual exact-byte helper nevertheless passed, so TRC-PF-01 is closed for the reviewed bytes.
